title: Create train variations within a theme by mode, complexity, persona, or phase

facts.note: Train definition files / train ids (e.g. train:<theme>:<variation> as in the source examples).
Creating new train variations or revising existing ones.

values: train variation added or revised (with a new or existing theme)
facts.note: Needs a diff observer that detects train variations being added or revised in train definitions, whether the theme is new or existing.
Task wording about train variations; task words alone do not establish applicability, so an LLM judges whether variations are being defined.

fires: Planner defines a new theme together with its train variations.
Planner adds a train variation under an existing theme.
Planner revises how an existing train variation is varied (e.g. changes its mode, complexity, persona or phase) without adding a new id.
doesNotFire: Editing code, tests, or docs that do not define or revise train variations.
Editing train content unrelated to how variations are created (e.g. fixing a typo in a step description).

given: A planner is defining or revising train variations for a theme (new or existing).
when: Creating or revising those train variations.
then: Create the train variations within the theme by mode, complexity, persona, or phase.
prefer: By mode, e.g. train:match:solo / train:match:duel / train:match:team.
By complexity, e.g. train:decision:core / train:decision:timeout / train:decision:preview.
By phase, e.g. train:league:tournament-setup / train:league:tournament-active / train:league:tournament-complete.
why: The source states no rationale; the four strategies are the canonical ways to vary trains within a theme.
evidence: Reviewer can relate each train variation under a theme to mode, complexity, persona, or phase (variation_strategy term: by_mode, by_complexity, by_persona, by_phase).
verifier_detail: Examples are illustrative only; they do not impose an identifier grammar or exclusivity of one strategy per variation.
